newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba says Feb M3 slowed by money cap formation.
newsitem.headline: Buba says Feb M3 slowed by money cap formation.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Wednesday that February M3 money supply growth slowed markedly from January's because of a rise in money capital formation.
Seasonally-adjusted, annualised M3 growth in February slowed to 9.1 percent from the final quarter of 1996 compared with growth of 11.7 percent in January.
M3 growth was also dampened by an outflow of funds in foreign transactions by domestic non-banks and by slowdown in bank lending to the public sector which was very high in January.
By contrast bank lending to companies and private individuals strengthened, albeit due in large measure to securities purchases by banks, the Bundesbank said in a statement.
The Bundesbank warned that any interpretation of the February and January M3 data must take into account that annualised growth rates were subject to swings at the beginning of the year.
The Bundesbank said that cash in circulation and standard savings deposits expanded strongly in February. Sight deposits also grew, but at a slower pace than in the two previous months.
Monetary capital formation, which in January virtually ceased, revived in February due mainly to increased investment by domestic non-banks in bank bonds, the Bundesbank said.
The non-annualised M3 growth rate in February advanced to 2.2 percent from January's 1.9 percent.
The Bundesbank said that compared with the final quarter of 1995, annualised M3 grew at an annualised rate of 8.3 percent in February, down from 8.6 percent in January.
